key_insight: Physics-anchored residual learning reduced compact QNN cloud-cover prediction error by 38.8–54.3% versus direct QNN prediction, but a stronger classical model remained more accurate.
engineering_relevance: Learning corrections to an existing physical estimate can improve compact QNN parameterizations without replacing the baseline model.
method: Retain a fitted cloud-cover estimate and learn a correction to its logit in transformed target space.
Evaluate six- and eight-input XYZ and ZZXY quantum circuits with local Z readout and noiseless exact expectations.
Compare direct and residual QNNs against compact residual MLP and larger Grundner-Q1 classical references.
evidence_signal: On released ICON/DYAMOND-derived data with three matched replicates and 10,000 training samples each, residual XYZ achieved mean test MSEs of 0.01124 and 0.01082 versus 0.00778 and 0.00791 for residual Q1.
watch_item: Noiseless offline simulations establish neither computational quantum advantage nor skill when coupled to an online climate model.
paper_title: Physics-anchored residual quantum neural networks for cloud-cover parameterization
